key_findings.finding: The key primary paper is PMID 25424483, “Statin treatment affects cytokine release and phagocytic activity in primary cultured microglia through two separable mechanisms” (Molecular Brain, 2014). It tested simvastatin in primary cultured rat microglia, using 20 μM as the effective non-toxic dose; treatment lowered cellular cholesterol by approximately 18%.

key_findings.finding: Simvastatin altered secretion of microglial mediators, specifically including IL-1β, TNF-α, and BDNF; the paper reports this secretory phenotype as cholesterol-dependent. TNF-α was not detectable under at least one reported condition, so cytokine-specific direction/magnitude should not be generalized beyond the paper’s detailed figures.

Simvastatin inhibited microglial phagocytosis, but this effect was cholesterol-independent. The authors therefore concluded that cytokine/trophic-factor release and phagocytosis are separable statin responses rather than one downstream consequence of cholesterol depletion.
